scope: phase_F_completeness; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Media answer can cite nonexistent page numbers that happen to exist in the visible page set, but cached/OCR page numbering is attacker-influenced and not re-verified against the source
findings.issue: When OCR runs, `extracted=self.ocr(asset,source)` replaces the page list without any validation that page numbers are positive integers, unique, or bounded, and later `question` computes `actual={page for page,body in extracted['pages']}` and only checks `cited<=actual`. A buggy or adversarial OCR adapter returning pages like `[[0,'x'],[-3,'y'],[999999999,'z']]` lets the model produce citations that pass validation, and the returned `page_refs` are unbounded integers with no relationship to the document.
findings.fix: Validate `extracted['pages']` after every producer (subprocess output and OCR): each entry must be a 2-element list `[int page, str text]`, pages strictly positive, unique, ascending, and <= the known page/asset bound; reject otherwise. Return only validated page refs.

findings.title: Post-extraction bound is checked on file size before JSON parsing, and parsed payload structure is not validated
findings.issue: `out.stat().st_size>64000` bounds the raw JSON file, but `json.loads` result is used unchecked: `extracted['pages']` can be any type or contain non-string bodies, and if the extractor output lacks the 'pages' key a KeyError surfaces instead of a typed storage error. Combined with the OCR substitution path, no validation enforces the structure the citation check depends on.
findings.fix: After `json.loads`, require a dict with a required 'pages' key of bounded length (e.g. <= 32) whose entries are `[int,str]` pairs, otherwise raise `StorageError('extraction output malformed')` before any OCR substitution or caching.

findings.title: OCR path returns unbound extraction result even when no authorization is granted for its content
findings.issue: When text-layer extraction yields only blank pages and `self.ocr` is provided, the code calls `self.ocr(asset,source)` unconditionally and returns or caches its output. If OCR invokes a remote provider (nothing in the supplied modules forbids that, since the adapter is injected), this sends user media to an external provider with no `AuthorizationRequest`, reservation, or accounting, unlike `extract`'s local vs egress distinction elsewhere. The comment on cache hits ('cache hits never substitute for model-egress consent') does not cover this path.
findings.fix: Restrict `self.ocr` to a local-only adapter interface that never performs network egress, or require an explicit `authorize_and_reserve` with a dedicated `media.ocr` capability/purpose before invoking OCR and record accounting; fail closed with `ocr_unavailable` when none is available.

findings.title: Domain import reapplies deleted-object tombstones via delete_derived_in that may resurrect derived state created after the snapshot
findings.issue: After replacing all domain tables with the source snapshot, `apply_domain_delta` runs `delete_derived_in` for every tombstone row. Because `delete_derived_in` cancels jobs, deletes conversation history, artifacts, cache entries and watch bindings matching those refs at import time, re-importing the same delta (as the repeated-import test exercises) is idempotent only where the derived data matches. However `delete_derived_in` also mutates `pa_memory.previews` and deletes object rows for descendants computed at import time; if the snapshot's dependency graph contains a descendant that the live target had legitimately re-created with a new version (same object_ref), that newer target state is silently deleted rather than surfaced as a conflict.
findings.fix: Before applying each tombstone, check for target-owned objects under that ref whose row data differs from what was tombstoned in the snapshot and raise a forward-fix conflict instead of deleting unconditionally; or restrict re-import tombstone reapplication to refs absent from the target object_versions table.

findings.title: Media download reservation is not tied to the request's ownership and can be triggered for another chat's file_ref
findings.issue: `download` validates `file_ref` only for length and authorizes against `self.resource_ref` set at construction time; there is no check that `file_ref` originated from the authenticated chat/user that owns `root.owner_ref`. A caller that forwards an arbitrary `file_id` can fetch any file Telegram exposes to the bot token, regardless of which owner/chat supplied it, and the bytes are then stored under the assistant's owner_ref.
findings.fix: Thread the authenticated chat/actor tuple through `download` and require it to match `root.owner_ref` (similar to `MemoryRuntime._owner`) before reserving, and record which chat/user supplied the `file_ref` in the resulting asset.

not_verified: Runtime behavior of `prm.storage.postgres` (PostgresStore/StateTransaction, `_object_lock`, `put`/`get` semantics) since that module is not in the supplied packet.
`prm.capabilities` reservation/grant enforcement and `authorize_and_reserve` semantics; assumed fail-closed but not source-verified here.
`reader.PrivateReportRuntime.cleanup_deleted` and `WatchScheduler.complete_subject_in` implementations referenced from deletion/migration code.
Whether injected `ocr`/`vision`/`transcriber` adapters in non-test production wiring perform their own network egress or scope checks.
Whether `pa_jobs.jobs.payload` input_namespace/input_ref keys are always present as strings (deletion relies on `payload->>'input_namespace'` string equality).
findings.summary: Overall this module set is carefully fail-closed: unknown/outcome-ambiguous media transports are fenced as non-retryable with durable model_attempt records, reservations are abandoned before transport on validation failures, unknown pricing stays NULL rather than zero, deletion applies owner-scoped tombstones plus artifact cleanup, and receipts/deltas are monotone against replays. The main remaining risks are around media extraction output validation and OCR substitution: extracted page structure and OCR-produced page numbering are trusted without schema checks, allowing bad citations and possibly mis-scoped egress through injected OCR adapters; migration also re-deletes descendant refs on repeated imports without conflict detection. None of these are P0 since they require an already-authorized owner-context or a faulty injected adapter to exploit, but they should be fixed before broadened use.
